podcast.title: Drumming Influence on Dave Grohl
podcast.body: Dave Grohl (Nirvana, Foo Fighters) expressed gratitude to Tony Thompson, acknowledging that he had "ripped off" Thompson's drumming style throughout his career, including on Nirvana's "Nevermind" album. Thompson's response was simply, "I know." "And Girl told Thompson, man, I just want to thank you because I owe you so much for ripping you off my whole life. And you know what Tony Thompson said? I know."

podcast.title: Gated Reverb Snare Demonstration
podcast.body: Drummer Tony Thompson's powerful snare hits effectively demonstrate the sound of a reverb gate maxing out, producing a distinct crackle that follows the initial crack of the drumstick. This technique was a signature element contributing to the big, powerful snare drum sound highly sought after in the 1980s. "You can actually hear the reverb gate max out when Tony Thompson hits his snare really, really hard. That's the crackle that comes after the crack of the stick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Distinctive Drum Sound
xref.body: A key characteristic of recordings from The Power Station was its unique drum sound, described as "big, powerful and boomed." This was achieved through the studio's special ambient acoustics, sometimes augmented with noise gates on kits like Tony Thompson's. "The biggest difference between the power station and just about everywhere else was how drums sounded."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Exemplar of 1980s Drum Sound
xref.body: The band, featuring Robert Palmer, members of Duran Duran, and drummer Tony Thompson, is highlighted as a prime example of the pervasive drum sound of the 1980s. This sound was characterized by its big, boomy, and powerful quality, often achieved by recording in large, reverberant rooms and augmenting with electronic effects like gated reverbs. "The Power Station featuring Robert Palmer, a couple of guys from Durandoran and drummer Tony Thompson. That is an example of the drum sound that was very much invoked in the 1980s."
